summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and multiple abdominal surgeries was admitted for acute epigastric pain, nausea, and bilious vomiting lasting four days, along with a report of black stool. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and guaiac-positive stool, but normal pancreatic enzymes and no evidence of bowel obstruction or pulmonary embolism on CT imaging. His acute kidney injury, likely pre-renal from dehydration, resolved with IV fluids. Pain improved with supportive care, and he was advanced to a regular diet. New right-sided numbness and weakness were noted but CT head showed no acute pathology. He was discharged home with improved symptoms, instructions to restart diabetes medications with adequate intake, and follow-up with his primary care provider.
